t: Appropriations in this title shall be available for expenses of attendance by military personnel at meetings in the manner authorized by 5 U.S.C. 4110, uniforms, and allowances therefor, as authorized by law (5 U.S.C. 5901–5902), and for printing, either during a recess or session of Congress, of survey reports authorized by law, and such survey reports as may be printed during a recess of Congress shall be printed, with illustrations, as documents of the next succeeding session of Congress; not to exceed $2,000 for official reception and representation expenses; and during the current fiscal year the revolving fund, Corps of Engineers, shall be available for purchase (not to exceed 221 of which 216 shall be for replacement only) and hire of passenger motor vehicles: Provided, That the total accrued expenditures of the capital investment program of the revolving fund shall not exceed $150,000,000 in fiscal year 1981.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "attendance ... at meetings" and the printing of survey reports as congressional documents signal public participation. But this is only an appropriations-availability provision: it funds federal military personnel attending meetings, uniforms, printing, reception expenses, and vehicle purchases. No party outside the federal government is consulted, heard, or given a right to challenge any federal decision, and the printing of reports for Congress stays inside the government.
fable.s: Appropriations in this title shall be available for expenses of attendance by military personnel at meetings in the manner authorized by 5 U.S.C. 4110

opus.w: This section only says what appropriated funds can pay for: travel to meetings, uniforms, printing, reception expenses and vehicles. The mention of military personnel attending meetings is about covering expenses, not about consulting people outside the government before a federal decision. Printing survey reports as documents of Congress also stays inside the federal government.
opus.s: Appropriations in this title shall be available for expenses of attendance by military personnel at meetings in the manner authorized by 5 U.S.C. 4110
opus.b: 1. **The tempting reading:** the words "attendance by military personnel at meetings" and the printing of survey reports "as documents of the next succeeding session of Congress" sound procedural. That reading fails. The meetings are just one kind of expense the money can pay for. Nothing here has outside parties advising on a federal decision, and printing reports for Congress stays inside the federal government. The section only says what the appropriations can be spent on, much like Example 1.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a standard appropriations clause detailing how funds can be spent on administrative items such as uniforms, vehicle purchases, printing reports for Congress, and reception expenses. It does not establish any process for consulting with or coordinating with parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. The mention of Congress is internal to the government, and reception expenses do not constitute a formal participation mechanism like a hearing or advisory committee.
qwen_chat.s: Appropriations in this title shall be available for expenses of attendance by military personnel at meetings in the manner authorized by 5 U.S.C. 4110, uniforms, and allowances therefor, as authorized by law (5 U.S.C. 5901–5902), and for printing, either during a recess or session of Congress, of survey reports authorized by law, and such survey reports as may be printed during a recess of Congress shall be printed, with illustrations, as documents of the next succeeding session of Congress; not to exceed $2,000 for official reception and representation expenses; and during the current fiscal year the revolving fund, Corps of Engineers, shall be available for purchase (not to exceed 221 of which 216 shall be for replacement only) and hire of passenger motor vehicles: Provided, That the total accrued expenditures of the capital investment program of the revolving fund shall not exceed $150,000,000 in fiscal year 1981.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "official reception and representation expenses" implies interaction with the public or outside entities, thus constituting participation. However, the definition explicitly excludes general administrative or operational expenses unless they involve a specific consultation, hearing, or advisory process with outside parties. Mere spending on receptions does not constitute a structured participation mechanism like a public comment period or advisory board. Furthermore, the printing of reports for Congress is an internal government action (Congress is inside the federal government).
